key.name: position
key.description: Which screen edge the taskbar sits on. Windows 11 keeps it at the bottom; on the left or right it stands upright and everything opens beside it.

key.name: taskbar-size
key.description: In logical pixels: the bar's height along the top or bottom, its width on a side. 48 is what was measured on Windows; the task buttons and Start follow it.

key.name: alignment
key.description: Centre matches Windows 11; left matches Windows 10.

key.name: reserve-space
key.summary: Reserve screen space for the taskbar
key.description: When off, maximised windows run underneath the bar and show through its acrylic surface.

key.name: auto-hide
key.description: When set, the taskbar no longer reserves screen space.

key.name: multi-monitor
key.description: Windows shows the taskbar on all displays by default.

key.name: isolate-monitors
key.summary: Only show windows from this display
key.description: Each taskbar lists only the windows on its own display.

key.name: isolate-workspaces
key.summary: Only show windows from the current workspace
key.description: Matches the Windows virtual-desktop default.

key.name: show-pinned
key.description: Pinned apps keep a button even when they are not running.

key.name: hide-top-panel
key.description: Windows has a single bar; hiding the top bar matches that.

key.name: search-style
key.description: As Windows offers it: hidden, the search icon only, the icon and its label, or a search box. A bar standing on a side shows only the icon. It opens Start with its search box ready.

key.name: clock-date-format
key.summary: strftime format for the clock's second line

key.name: aero-peek
key.summary: Peek at a window when hovering its thumbnail
key.description: Fades the other windows out, as Aero Peek does.

key.name: quick-links-key
key.description: Windows' Win+X menu, also on a right-click of the Start button.

key.name: clipboard-history
key.description: Remembers what you copy and offers it back at the pointer, as Win+V does.

key.name: clipboard-paste
key.description: Types the paste shortcut into the window that had focus, as Windows does. Turn off to only put it on the clipboard. Terminals get Ctrl+Shift+V.

key.name: clipboard-pinned
key.description: Kept across restarts, as Windows keeps pinned items.

key.name: snap-layouts-key
key.summary: Open the snap layouts over the focused window

key.name: snap-layouts
key.description: Windows 11's snap layouts: Win+Z over a window, the bar at the top of the screen while a window is dragged there, a half or a quarter of the screen for a window dragged to a side or a corner, the whole of it at the top, and snap assist for the zones left over. GNOME's own tiling at the edges is off meanwhile; while Ubuntu's Tiling Assistant is on, the edges are left to it.

key.name: snap-restore-edge-tiling
key.summary: GNOME's edge tiling to switch back on
key.description: Set while the snap layouts have switched GNOME's tiling at the screen edges off, so that it is switched back on when they stop.

key.name: super-number-keys
key.description: As on Windows. GNOME binds these to the favourites list instead, which disagrees as soon as something unpinned is running; its binding is restored when this is off.

key.name: yielded-bindings
key.summary: GNOME key bindings set aside for the Windows shortcuts
key.description: Internal. Maps "schema key" to the value it had before a Windows shortcut took one of its accelerators, so that it can be given back on disable — including after a session that ended without one.

key.name: context-menu-on-release
key.summary: Open context menus on release, not on press
key.description: Windows opens a right-click menu when the button comes back up. Opening it on press breaks right-drag gestures, which some applications rely on.

key.name: icon-size
key.description: 24 is what was measured on Windows. Larger reads better on a high-density display where the bar looks sparse. This is the size on a 48px bar; a thicker or thinner bar (taskbar-size) scales it.

key.name: theme
key.description: Follow the desktop setting, or pin the taskbar to light or dark independently of it.

key.name: acrylic
key.summary: Blur the desktop behind the taskbar
key.description: Approximates the acrylic material Windows uses.

key.name: hide-overview-dash
key.description: The taskbar already shows the same apps.

key.name: start-layout
key.description: Compact six-column layout, the larger eight-column Insider layout, or a size of your own (start-width × start-height).

key.name: start-width
key.description: In logical pixels. Used when start-layout is custom; the pinned grid takes as many 96px columns as fit.

key.name: start-height
key.description: In logical pixels. Used when start-layout is custom; the extra height goes to more rows of pinned apps.

key.name: start-pinned
key.description: Independent of the taskbar's pinned apps (GNOME favourites), as on Windows. Edited from Start's own context menu.

key.name: start-pins-initialized
key.summary: Whether Start's pins have been seeded
key.description: Internal. Start is seeded once with common apps; after that an emptied list stays empty.

key.name: start-folders
key.description: Selected folder and application ids, configured in preferences.

key.name: tray-hover
key.summary: What hovering a tray icon shows
key.description: A program menu when available, a Windows-style tooltip, or nothing.

key.name: start-menu
key.description: When off, the Start button opens GNOME's app grid.

key.name: super-opens-start
key.summary: The Super key opens the Start menu
key.description: Matches the Windows key. When off, Super opens GNOME's Overview as usual.

key.name: show-tray
key.description: Hosts StatusNotifierItem tray icons in the taskbar.

key.name: show-input-method
key.description: Display the current Fcitx input method or GNOME keyboard source.

key.name: show-system-indicators
key.summary: Move GNOME's Quick Settings into the taskbar
key.description: Windows keeps network, volume and battery in the tray; with the top bar hidden these have to live here.

key.name: gtk-window-style
key.summary: Windows 11 title bars for GTK apps
key.description: Writes a marked block into ~/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css and ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css: Windows' caption buttons and 8px corners for every GTK app, and Minimise and Maximise in GNOME's button layout. Turning it off, or turning the extension off, takes them away again.

key.name: gtk-mica
key.description: With the Windows title bars on: the wallpaper, blurred and washed with the theme's colour, shows through a GTK window's title bar and background, as Windows 11's Mica does; windows that are not active show the plain colour.

key.name: gtk-window-style-layout
key.summary: GNOME's button layout before the GTK title bars changed it

key.name: window-frames
key.description: Windows that draw no shadow of their own — Electron, Chromium with its own title bar, Qt, undecorated windows — get Windows 11's 8px corners, its 1px edge and its shadow. GTK windows draw their own and are left alone.

key.name: window-animations
key.description: Windows open, close, minimise and restore the way Windows 11 animates them: growing out of their centre, shrinking into their taskbar button. Off leaves GNOME's own animations.

key.name: flash-attention
key.description: An app whose window asks for attention flashes its taskbar button seven times and keeps it lit until the window is used, as Windows does, instead of GNOME's "is ready" notification.

key.name: quick-settings-editable
key.summary: Allow editing the quick settings panel
key.description: Adds the edit button Windows has, for choosing which tiles the panel shows.

key.name: quick-settings-hidden
key.summary: Quick settings tiles removed from the panel
key.description: Keyed by the tile's class and title. Edit the panel from its own edit button rather than by hand.

key.name: quick-settings-order
key.summary: The order of the quick settings tiles
key.description: Keyed as quick-settings-hidden is. Tiles not listed come after the rest. Drag the tiles in the panel's edit mode rather than editing this by hand.

key.name: tray-hidden-items
key.summary: Tray items folded into the overflow
key.description: Ids of StatusNotifierItems shown behind the chevron instead of directly in the taskbar.

key.name: debug-service
key.summary: Expose a read-only D-Bus service for geometry tests
key.description: Used by tools/verify-geometry.py to diff the rendered taskbar against the Windows measurements.

key.name: jumplist-recent
key.summary: Show recent documents in the jump list
